subject.title: Add maxThreads config for local embedding (node-llama-cpp)

question: Should OpenClaw add an official `memorySearch.local.maxThreads` config knob for the llama.cpp embedding provider, or keep CPU thread tuning outside canonical config?
rationale: The implementation path is narrow and dependency-backed, but repository policy treats new config/default surfaces as product/API decisions.

options.title: Approve a narrow maxThreads knob
options.body: Add an optional advanced `memorySearch.local.maxThreads` field, leave the default undefined, and forward it only to `getLlama` for the official local provider.

options.title: Reject the config expansion
options.body: Keep current local embedding defaults and direct users needing deeper CPU tuning to external providers or custom plugin ownership.

options.title: Defer to broader local tuning design
options.body: Hold this issue until maintainers decide a complete local llama tuning surface that also covers GPU, NUMA, and related runtime options.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow maxThreads knob
recommendation.body: Add an optional advanced `memorySearch.local.maxThreads` field, leave the default undefined, and forward it only to `getLlama` for the official local provider.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a canonical config-surface and local-provider boundary choice, and recent history places steipete on those exact files.
